official.tuition_coverage_note: The scholarship provides '$50,000 scholarship towards their course fees and other university costs'. Funds are held by the universities and applied against successful applicants' fee and tuition accounts after the University census date for the semester applied for; each University decides the frequency and value of credit towards course fees, and payments are exclusive of GST.
benefits: $50,000 scholarship towards course fees and other university costs
Ten scholarships awarded each year - two successful international students at each of Western Australia's five universities
Scholarship funds are held by the university and applied against the recipient's fee and tuition account after the university census date for the semester applied for
Payments are exclusive of GST; each university decides the frequency and value of credit towards course fees
eligibility: New offshore enrolment into an undergraduate or postgraduate course (as specified by the chosen university) at one of Western Australia's 5 universities: Curtin University, Edith Cowan University, Murdoch University, The University of Notre Dame (Fremantle Campus), and The University of Western Australia

Citizen of one of the listed countries: Bangladesh, Bhutan, Brazil, China, Colombia, Hong Kong, India, Indonesia, Japan, Kenya, Malaysia, Nepal, Oman, the Philippines, Republic of Korea (South Korea), Saudi Arabia, Singapore, Sri Lanka, the United Arab Emirates, the United Kingdom or Vietnam

Commencing directly into the undergraduate or postgraduate program (not via a packaged, foundation or English language pathway) in the semester applied for; the 2026 Guidelines require full-time studies of a minimum of two years

Prepared to decline any other scholarships previously granted by the University, State or Commonwealth if their conditions prohibit holding multiple scholarships; must not be a recipient of another Western Australian Government scholarship
International fee-paying student on an Australian student visa (subclass 500); attendance confirmed past the census date for the semester applied for at payment date
Domestic students, onshore international students and citizens of unlisted countries are not eligible; eligibility criteria, including markets, are subject to annual review
requirements: Apply directly to the chosen Western Australian university via the university's official website when the round opens
Meet the eligibility criteria published in the application form on the chosen university's website
Submit the application within that university's scholarship window for the current round
documents: Academic records, as assessed by the chosen university
Responses to qualitative questions contained in the university's application
Supporting documents specified by the chosen university (each university determines the documentation required)
selection_criteria: Demonstration of a high-level of academic achievement as determined by the admitting university
Additional qualitative assessment by individual universities, which may request short-listed applicants to provide written or interview responses
coverage: Course fees and other university costs, credited against the recipient's fee and tuition account after the university census date for the semester applied for
No living cost, travel or installation allowance is published for this scholarship
application_method: Watch wa.gov.au and the five participating universities' pages for the opening of the next round
Visit the chosen university's application page when applications open and complete the university's online scholarship application
The university assesses applications against the published criteria and selects its successful students, then informs the Department
Successful applicants are notified by the university, followed by correspondence from the Western Australian Government once the student has passed the census date
official.application_route: Apply directly through one of the five participating Western Australian universities' official websites within that university's window when the round opens - not through the Department.
official.citizenship_residency: Citizen of one of the 21 listed countries (Bangladesh, Bhutan, Brazil, China, Colombia, Hong Kong, India, Indonesia, Japan, Kenya, Malaysia, Nepal, Oman, the Philippines, Republic of Korea (South Korea), Saudi Arabia, Singapore, Sri Lanka, the United Arab Emirates, the United Kingdom or Vietnam); must be a new international enrolment - domestic students and onshore international students are not eligible.
official.international_eligibility: International students only; domestic students and onshore international students are not eligible.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Undergraduate or postgraduate program at one of the five named Western Australian universities (each university determines which levels of study are eligible); entry via a packaged, foundation or English language pathway program is not eligible.
official.duration: One year (the Program provides up to 10 one-year scholarships valued annually at $50,000 each; recipients must undertake full-time study of at least two years)
official.description: The Western Australian Premier's University Scholarship is a Western Australian Government award, managed by the Department of Energy and Economic Diversification, that provides 10 successful students with a $50,000 scholarship towards their course fees and other university costs. It is designed to attract two high-achieving international students to each of Western Australia's five universities each year, with the application, evaluation and decision process administered by each university.
official.program_type: State government scholarship, administered by the participating universities

not_confirmed: Semester 1, 2027 (Round 8) application opening and closing dates - the Department states these are not yet published
Program-level English language requirement - not published by the Department; set by each participating university
University-level document lists and qualitative questions - each university determines these when its round opens
verification.notes: Amount ($50,000 AUD), annual round structure, eligible-country list, payment mechanics (fee account credit after census date, GST-exclusive) and the closed Semester 2, 2026 round were confirmed on the Department's program page, its Semester 2, 2026 application-information publication (both wa.gov.au, last updated 4 March 2026 and 29 May 2026) and the official 2026 Guidelines PDF linked from that page. The program page describes awards as being made 'each year to 2026' while also inviting applicants to watch for the Semester 1, 2027 round, so the 2027 continuation should be reconfirmed when announced.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a WA Government award run through the five participating universities rather than a central application: you apply directly to your chosen university when its round opens, and only two students per university are funded each year. The $50,000 is credited to your university fee account after the census date, so it reduces what you owe the university rather than paying you money. As at 10 October 2026 the Round 8 (Semester 1, 2027) dates were not published, so monitor wa.gov.au and the five universities' scholarship pages rather than relying on fixed calendar dates.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High-achieving new international students from the 21 listed countries starting a full-time undergraduate or postgraduate degree at Curtin, ECU, Murdoch, Notre Dame (Fremantle) or UWA in the round's semester.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your nationality is on the 21-country list and that you meet your chosen university's own entry requirements before the round opens
Shortlist one or two of the five universities and bookmark their scholarship pages to catch the Round 8 opening date
Prepare academic transcripts and draft answers to likely qualitative questions in case you are short-listed for a written or interview assessment
Budget for the whole course - the award is one year only and living costs, flights and visa costs are not covered
Check you hold no other WA Government scholarship and can decline other awards whose conditions prohibit holding multiple scholarships
common_rejection_risks: Sending an application to the Department instead of the university - direct applications to DEED are not assessed
Missing a university's own window, which can open and close inside the Department's round dates
Being a domestic student, an onshore international student, or a citizen of a country not on the list
Holding another WA Government scholarship or an award whose conditions forbid holding multiple scholarships
Starting via a packaged, foundation or English language pathway instead of direct entry into the degree
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Everything the $50,000 fee credit does not absorb: tuition beyond the one funded year, living costs in Perth, flights, student visa and Overseas Student Health Cover costs.
document_audit: Each university defines its own document list - do not assume transcripts alone are sufficient
Qualitative written or interview responses may only be requested at shortlist stage, so keep prepared answers ready
Depending on the university, academic records may need certified translations or supporting statements
alerts: Round 8 (Semester 1, 2027) dates were not published as at 10 October 2026 - the Department says to check back for updates
The program page states scholarships are awarded 'each year to 2026', so confirm the program's continuation for 2027 before relying on it
Eligibility criteria, including the market list, are subject to annual review
The scholarship cannot be postponed to a future semester - you must commence in the semester you applied for
Payment requires attendance confirmed past the census date and an Australian student visa (subclass 500) at payment date
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Wait for your chosen university to publish its round application page, apply through that university's online process inside its window, and the university notifies the Department of its two selections; the $50,000 is credited to your fee account after census.

official.deadline_note: CDU publishes two closing dates on its international student scholarships page: Semester 1, 2027 closes 31 January 2027 and Semester 2, 2027 closes 4 July 2027. No separate opening date for the scholarship application is published.
official.application_cycle: Semester 1, 2027 intake (applications close 31 January 2027); Semester 2, 2027 intake (applications close 4 July 2027)
official.status_note: CDU's international student scholarships page lists open application windows for the Semester 1, 2027 and Semester 2, 2027 intakes with closing dates of 31 January 2027 and 4 July 2027 respectively as at 10 October 2026.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The scholarship 'applies to an undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree covering 50% of the tuition fee for the full duration of the course'. The recipient pays the remaining portion of tuition on or before the payment due date (first day of teaching) of each semester.
official.funding_period: % of tuition fee, full duration of the course
benefits: 50% of the tuition fee for an undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree, for the full duration of the course
Neither transferable for cash nor refundable, and cannot be transferred to another person, semester, course or year
Results are announced during Orientation Week, before teaching starts
eligibility: Applicant must apply to commence study in Semester 1 or Semester 2 2027 (the intake they are offered first)
Applicant must meet the University's academic and English language entry requirements for their chosen course
Applicant must have a minimum overall score of 95% in their highest completed qualification
Applicant must be an international student paying international student fees
Applicant must not hold another scholarship from an Australian or foreign sponsoring agency
The scholarship applies to an undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree
requirements: Step 1: Apply to study at CDU
Step 2: Submit your application for the VCIHAS
The application form requires the application intake, an Application Number (StudyLink or SATAC), and an email address matching the one provided in the StudyLink application
The form requires the average overall score in the highest completed qualification, expressed as a percentage

The applicant statement (why you should be selected; how you will become an outstanding ambassador of CDU; extracurricular activities focused on community engagement, work experience, creative arts and sport; how you will use your CDU qualification to make a difference in your community) is mandatory

The declaration must be ticked (information true and correct; conditions understood; competitive process with the decision of the University selection panel final; no more than one tuition fee scholarship held from CDU at a time; no other scholarship from an Australian or foreign sponsorship agency; possible student story or testimonial) and the form signed and dated
documents: Application intake selection and Application Number (StudyLink or SATAC)
Email address as provided in the StudyLink application
Average overall score in the highest completed qualification, given as a percentage
Applicant statement answering the four published questions (the scholarship page states up to 600 words; the application form states 500 words or less)
selection_criteria: Overall score in the highest completed qualification
Supporting statement outlining why you should be awarded a scholarship
coverage: 50% of the tuition fee for an undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree, for the full duration of the course
The recipient pays the remaining portion of the tuition fees on or before the payment due date (first day of teaching) of each semester
application_method: Apply to study at CDU and obtain an Application Number (StudyLink or SATAC)
Use the same email address in the scholarship form as in the StudyLink application
Complete the Vice-Chancellor's High Achievers Scholarship (VCIHAS) Application form, including intended intake, average overall score as a percentage, and the four applicant statement questions
Tick the declaration, sign the form and enter the date, then submit before the closing date for the intake (31 January 2027 for Semester 1, 2027 or 4 July 2027 for Semester 2, 2027)
Await the outcome - CDU states results will be announced during Orientation Week
official.application_route: Apply to study at CDU first, then submit the VCIHAS application form using the same email address as your StudyLink application.
official.study_mode: Full-time (a full-time enrolment of 40 credit points (0.5 EFTSL) each semester is required to retain the scholarship)
official.citizenship_residency: Open to international students paying international student fees; no country restrictions are published for this scholarship.
official.international_eligibility: International students only - the applicant must be an international student liable for international student fees.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree only; the applicant must not hold another scholarship from an Australian or foreign sponsoring agency and cannot hold more than one tuition fee scholarship from CDU at a time.
official.duration: The minimum time in which the course can be completed, or until the earliest of: the maximum scholarship value has been exhausted, the course is completed, or the recipient no longer meets the ongoing eligibility of the scholarship.
official.description: The Vice-Chancellor's International High Achievers Scholarship is a Charles Darwin University award for international students with a record of academic excellence. CDU offers a limited number of these scholarships, covering 50% of the tuition fee for an undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree for the full duration of the course, assessed on the overall score in the applicant's highest completed qualification plus a supporting statement.
official.region: Northern Territory, Australia (CDU Darwin; catalogue region: Oceania)
official.english_requirement: Applicants must meet the University's academic and English language entry requirements for their chosen course and supply evidence at the time of application. Published minimum English test scores for most CDU higher education courses: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (postgraduate) or 6.0 (undergraduate) with no band below 6.0; PTE Academic overall 58 or 50 with no score below 50; TOEFL overall 79 or 60 with a minimum writing score of 21; Cambridge English: Advanced overall 176 or 169 with no skill below 169; Duolingo overall 120 or 110 (accepted until 14 August 2027); CDU ELICOS EAP004 (postgraduate) or EAP003 (undergraduate). Approved tests must be completed within two years of commencement; IELTS One Skill Retake is accepted. Alternative evidence routes: Year 12 in an approved English-speaking country, 0.5 FTE of higher education study in an approved country, an enabling course, a TAFE qualification at Certificate III or higher, current AHPRA registration, two years of full-time equivalent English-medium employment, or a primary language pathway declaration. Nursing and midwifery courses require higher scores under AHPRA rules.

not_confirmed: Opening date for VCIHAS applications - CDU publishes closing dates only
Whether an interview applies to VCIHAS - the scholarship page publishes no interview requirement (interviews are published for other CDU International College scholarships)
The maximum scholarship value in dollars - only the 50% tuition rate is published, so no dollar amount is recorded
verification.notes: The 50% tuition coverage, eligibility criteria, selection criteria, duration and ongoing eligibility terms, closing dates (31 January 2027 for Semester 1, 2027 and 4 July 2027 for Semester 2, 2027) and the two-step application route were confirmed on CDU's international student scholarships page; the form fields, declaration and statement word limit were confirmed on the VCIHAS application page; English minimums were confirmed on CDU's English language proficiency page. The official pages disagree on the statement length (up to 600 words on the scholarship page versus 500 words or less on the application form).

applicant_utility.summary: VCIHAS halves your tuition for the whole course, but you must fund the other 50% yourself and CDU requires your share by the first day of teaching each semester. The hard gate is a 95% or higher overall score in your highest completed qualification - below that the application is not competitive. The process is two-step: first apply to study at CDU to get a StudyLink or SATAC application number, then submit the separate VCIHAS form using the same email address as your course application.
applicant_utility.best_fit: International applicants with a 95% or higher overall score in their highest completed qualification who are applying to commence an undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree at CDU in Semester 1 or Semester 2 2027 and can pay the remaining 50% of tuition themselves.
application_readiness_checklist: Apply to study at CDU first and note your StudyLink or SATAC application number and the exact email address you used

Draft the four-part applicant statement (reasons for selection, CDU ambassadorship, extracurricular activities with community engagement, work experience, creative arts and sport, and community impact) within the word limit
Tick the declaration, sign the form and enter the date - unsigned or undated forms are incomplete
Confirm which statement length applies - the scholarship page says up to 600 words and the form says 500 or less - with CDU before submitting
Plan how you will pay the remaining 50% of tuition by the first day of teaching each semester
common_rejection_risks: Submitting the VCIHAS form before you have a course application and Application Number
Using a different email address in the scholarship form than in the StudyLink application
An average overall score below 95% in the highest completed qualification
Holding another scholarship from an Australian or foreign sponsoring agency, or another CDU tuition fee scholarship
Missing the 31 January 2027 (Semester 1) or 4 July 2027 (Semester 2) closing date, or applying for an intake other than the one you are first offered
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The remaining 50% of tuition fees, living costs in Darwin, Overseas Student Health Cover, flights and student visa costs - the award is a tuition reduction only and cannot be redeemed for cash.
document_audit: The average overall score must be entered as a percentage, not as a GPA or grade
Signature and date are required fields on the application form
The statement must answer four specific questions - a generic personal statement misses the brief
The published word limits conflict (600 words on the scholarship page, 500 words or less on the form) - confirm the applicable limit with CDU
alerts: To retain the scholarship you must keep a minimum GPA of 5.3 with no fail grade in any unit and a full-time enrolment of 40 credit points (0.5 EFTSL) each semester unless a reduced load or leave of absence is approved
The award ends at the earliest of: maximum scholarship value exhausted, course completion, or loss of ongoing eligibility
It is neither transferable for cash nor refundable and cannot be transferred to another person, semester, course or year
You must be able to pay your portion of tuition on or before the first day of teaching of each semester, and results are only announced during Orientation Week - plan cash flow accordingly
Only one CDU tuition fee scholarship may be held at a time, so this award cannot be stacked with another CDU tuition scholarship
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply to study at CDU through StudyLink or SATAC, then submit the VCIHAS application form with your application number, percentage score and signed statement before your intake's closing date; CDU announces results during Orientation Week.
